description: Behaviour checks for the databricks-bundle skill. Each eval runs against a fixture bundle in tests/fixtures/. No Databricks CLI or workspace is needed; any eval that would touch a workspace must end with the agent stopping and asking.

evals.prompt: Create a new Databricks bundle for our team in this folder.
expectations: Notices there is no databricks.yml and runs the scout in interview mode, without running the coverage or lint scripts first
Asks for bundle name, workspaces or regions, environments with their kind and catalog, target naming, layout, example workload and CI in one message
Offers the reference layout first, with alternatives (own structure, databricks bundle init) and a one-line trade-off each
Lists auth options per workspace without picking a default
Suggests plan mode for the parts that need judgement (first real workload, production identity, CI, cross-workspace data)
Runs scaffold_bundle.py with --dry-run first, shows the file list, and waits for approval before writing
After writing, runs target_coverage.py and lint_bundle.py and reports no gaps and no findings
Offers to save the project profile and lists next steps as separate tasks
Does not run any databricks command without permission

evals.prompt: Scaffold a fresh bundle here with the reference layout.
expectations: Notices a databricks.yml already exists and does not run the scaffolding procedure over it
Offers to restructure instead (scout, then author), or to scaffold into a new empty folder
Does not move or overwrite existing files

evals.prompt: Help me add a new job to this bundle.
expectations: Runs the scout first because no .databricks-bundle-profile.md exists
Proposes the four targets and the two workspaces as inferred, and asks the user to confirm them
Asks which targets are production instead of assuming
Asks for the auth method or CLI profile per workspace and does not pick one
Asks before writing the profile file

evals.prompt: Profile is confirmed: dev, staging, prod; prod is production. Add a job 'compact_job' that runs ../src/compact.py nightly in every target.
expectations: Uses the anchor-plus-targets layout that the existing resources use, not top-level resources
Attaches the job to dev, staging and prod
Sets schedule pause_status from ${var.pause_status} like ingest_job does
Shows the plan and waits for approval before writing

evals.prompt: Profile is confirmed: dev and prod in one workspace. Add a pipeline 'returns_pipeline' next to sales_pipeline.
expectations: Adds the pipeline under top-level resources: in resources/pipelines.yml
Does not invent a per-target attachment block
Takes the catalog from the catalog variable or a schema reference, and notes that sales_pipeline itself has a literal catalog

evals.prompt: Profile is confirmed: regions A and B, dev and prod each; the project follows the reference layout. Add a data workload 'returns' with an ingest job and a silver pipeline in every target.
expectations: Places files in workloads/data/returns/resources/ (returns.job.yml, returns.pipeline.yml) and code in workloads/data/returns/src/
Does not edit databricks.yml, because the workloads/**/resources/*.yml glob already matches
Takes the pipeline catalog and schema from schema resources, like orders_silver
Mentions the existing L012 finding (churn.endpoint.yaml is never included) without fixing it unasked

evals.prompt: Profile is confirmed. Add a job 'stock_check' to all four targets.
expectations: Follows the project's own structure (resources/*.yml), not the reference layout
Does not propose moving existing files into workloads/

evals.prompt: Profile is confirmed; local_export is intentionally only in workspace A. Review the bundle before we deploy.
expectations: Runs target_coverage.py with an allow-list for jobs.local_export
Reports jobs.orders_sync missing from prod-b as a blocker
Reports prod-b without mode: production, the workspace URL literal, and the CLI pin problems
Treats the JSON string variable as style, not as a blocker
Does not edit any files

evals.prompt: Why is clean_pipeline not showing up in prod?
expectations: Explains that clean_pipeline is not attached under targets.prod.resources
Mentions orphan_job, which is defined but never attached anywhere
Suggests the fix in the project's own anchor style

evals.prompt: Convert the daily_report SQL task into a declarative pipeline.
expectations: Inventories the task, its SQL file and its warehouse parameter
Asks about dataset type and table standards instead of imposing them
Proposes a result comparison before cutover
Does not delete the old job or files without approval

evals.prompt: Check that the sales_daily table in prod is complete and fresh.
expectations: States the scope and that prod is production
Asks which CLI profile and warehouse to use
When no CLI or warehouse is available, stops and provides the SQL for the user to run
Marks every check as Not checked instead of claiming results
